Convert a DNA alignment into a TreePPL integer matrix

Source: R/data.R
tp_dna_to_int.Rd

Recodes an alignment as integers, taxa in rows and sites in columns: A = 0, C = 1, G = 2, T = 3. Every other symbol (gaps -, ?, N and IUPAC ambiguity codes) becomes missing. Pass the result to tp_write_tppl_json() after unname() to get an Int[][].

Usage

tp_dna_to_int(aln, missing = 4L)

Arguments

aln

A DNA alignment of class DNAbin, as returned by ape::read.FASTA() or ape::read.dna(). All sequences must have the same length.

missing

Integer code used for any symbol other than A, C, G or T.

Value

An integer matrix with taxon names as row names.

Details

The missing-data code depends on the model: the tree-inference models use 4L (the default) and the phenotype-molecular model (qt.tppl) uses -1L.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
aln <- ape::read.FASTA("alignment.fasta")
tp_dna_to_int(aln) # tree-inference models
tp_dna_to_int(aln, missing = -1L) # qt model
} # }
